solutions.question: 1(a)
solutions.latex: $A = \displaystyle\int_b^0 f(x)\,dx - \int_0^a f(x)\,dx$, so the answer is D.

solutions.question: 1(b)
solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 12x - 3x^2$. Stationary points occur when $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$:

$0 = 12x - 3x^2 = 3x(4-x)$, so $x = 0, 4$.

When $x=0$, $y=0$. When $x=4$, $y = 6\times 4^2 - 4^3 = 32$.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} x & -1 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline \dfrac{dy}{dx} & -15 & 0 & 9 & 0 & -15 \end{array}$$

Slope pattern: decreasing, flat, increasing, flat, decreasing. So there is a maximum turning point at $(4,32)$ and a minimum turning point at $(0,0)$.

Alternate: $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 12 - 6x$. At $x=0$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 12$ (concave up). At $x=4$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -12$ (concave down).
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct x-coordinates of stationary points; 1: y-coordinates of stationary points; 1: determining nature of stationary points; if only 1 stationary point correctly identified (including its nature): 2 marks

solutions.question: 1(b)
solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 12 - 6x$. Setting $0 = 12 - 6x$ gives $x = 2$. When $x=2$, $y = 6\times 2^2 - 2^3 = 16$. Possible point of inflexion at $(2,16)$.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & 0 & 2 & 4 \\ \hline \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} & 12 & 0 & -12 \end{array}$$

Concave up, then concave down: the concavity changes, so there is a point of inflexion at $(2,16)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: identifying point of inflexion; 1: showing concavity change

solutions.question: 3(a)
solutions.latex: Reflection about the $y$-axis: $(-4, 6)$. Horizontal dilation, scale factor $\tfrac12$: $(-2, 6)$. Vertical translation up 2: $(-2, 8)$. So the answer is A.

solutions.question: 3(b)
solutions.latex:
$A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h$ and $V = 20 = \pi r^2 h$, so $h = \dfrac{20}{\pi r^2}$.

$$A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r\times\dfrac{20}{\pi r^2} = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{40}{r}$$

solutions.question: 3(b)
solutions.latex:
$A = 2\pi r^2 + 40r^{-1}$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 4\pi r - 40r^{-2} = 4\pi r - \dfrac{40}{r^2}$.

Set $0 = 4\pi r - \dfrac{40}{r^2}$: $\dfrac{40}{r^2} = 4\pi r$, so $\dfrac{10}{\pi} = r^3$ and $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{10}{\pi}}$.

$$\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} = 4\pi + 80r^{-3} = 4\pi + \dfrac{80}{r^3}$$

When $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{10}{\pi}}$: $\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} = 4\pi + \dfrac{80}{\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{10}{\pi}}\right)^3} = 37.6\ldots > 0$, so $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{10}{\pi}}$ gives a minimum surface area.

Alternate:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} r & 1 & \sqrt[3]{10/\pi} & 2 \\ \hline \dfrac{dA}{dr} & -27.4\ldots & 0 & 15.13\ldots \end{array}$$

Slope pattern: decreasing, flat, increasing, so minimum surface area occurs when $r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{10}{\pi}}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct differentiation; 1: correct value of $r$; 1: showing $r=\sqrt[3]{10/\pi}$ is a minimum value

solutions.question: 4(a)
solutions.latex: $f''(1) < 0$ as the curve is concave down. $f'(1) > 0$ as the tangent line has positive slope. $f'(1) < f(1)$ as the tangent line's $y$-intercept is positive. Hence $f''(1) < 0 < f'(1) < f(1)$, so the answer is D.

solutions.question: 4(c)
solutions.latex:
$y = 3 + \dfrac{1}{x+2}$. Vertical asymptote $x = -2$; horizontal asymptote $y = 3$.

When $x = 0$, $y = 3 + \dfrac12 = \dfrac72$.

When $y = 0$: $0 = 3 + \dfrac{1}{x+2}$, so $-3 = \dfrac{1}{x+2}$, $-3x - 6 = 1$, $x = -\dfrac73$.

\exfigure{1595_q4c_s1}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct asymptotes; 1: correct intercepts; 1: correct shape

solutions.question: 4(d)
solutions.latex: Exactly 3 solutions means $y = k$ intersects $y = f(x)$ 3 times, so $-2 < k < 5$.
